variations.name: CO2 trunk pipelines and regional aggregation networks
variations.description: Large-diameter pipelines (new-build or converted natural gas lines) gather CO2 from clusters of emitters and move it in dense phase to storage hubs; pipelines are by far the cheapest way to move large CO2 volumes onshore, making them the binding constraint on most CCS buildouts — and the most politically contested piece (eminent domain, siting).

companies.name: Kinder Morgan
companies.what: Operates the largest legacy US CO2 pipeline network (~1,500 miles incl. Cortez) feeding Permian EOR, the template for CO2 trunk economics.
companies.signal: Decades of operations moving >1 Bcf/d of CO2; positioning network for 45Q sequestration service

companies.name: ExxonMobil (Low Carbon Solutions)
companies.what: Owns the ~1,300-mile Denbury CO2 pipeline system on the Gulf Coast and is building it into an open CCS-as-a-service network for industrial emitters.
companies.signal: Acquired Denbury for $4.9B (Nov 2023); >5 Mtpa of third-party CO2 offtake contracts (CF Industries, Linde, Nucor)

companies.name: Summit Carbon Solutions
companies.what: Developing a ~2,500-mile Midwest trunk network aggregating CO2 from 50+ ethanol plants for North Dakota storage — the largest proposed CO2 pipeline in the world.
companies.signal: Raised >$1B (Continental Resources, TPG Rise, SK); Iowa permit 2024 but SD permit denied twice + 2025 SD eminent-domain ban; ND storage permit voided by court Mar 2026; rerouting west via Nebraska to Wyoming (May 2026)

companies.name: Navigator CO2 Ventures
companies.what: BlackRock-backed developer of the 1,300-mile Heartland Greenway ethanol CO2 pipeline across five Midwest states.
companies.signal: Cancelled the entire project Oct 2023 after permit denials in SD and IL opposition; company wound down — the marquee CO2 pipeline failure

companies.name: Wolf Midstream
companies.what: Owns and operates the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line (240 km, ~14.6 Mtpa design capacity — world's largest-capacity CO2 pipeline) and is expanding Edmonton-area connections.
companies.signal: ACTL operating since 2020; US affiliate Wolf Carbon Solutions withdrew its Iowa/Illinois pipeline applications (2023-24) after opposition

companies.name: Tallgrass Energy
companies.what: Converted the 392-mile Trailblazer natural gas line to CO2 service (Nebraska ethanol belt to its Eastern Wyoming sequestration hub) — proving brownfield conversion beats greenfield permitting.
companies.signal: ~$1.5B project in commercial CO2 service Sept 2025; ADM Columbus volumes flowing Nov 2025; >10 Mtpa capacity; new open season May 2026

companies.name: Gasunie
companies.what: Dutch state gas TSO building the Porthos CO2 collection pipeline/compressor for Rotterdam and co-developing the ~22 Mtpa Aramis offshore trunkline; already runs the OCAP CO2 line to greenhouses.
companies.signal: Porthos operational 2026; Aramis FID targeted 2026 with €639M Dutch state support; Gasunie/EBN to own the trunkline 50/50

variations.name: CO2 shipping (liquefied CO2 carriers with port liquefaction/buffer terminals)
variations.description: CO2 is liquefied and buffered at port terminals, then moved in pressurized refrigerated carriers to offshore storage hubs — giving dispersed coastal emitters access to storage without dedicated pipelines, and creating a flexible cross-border CO2 market (now recognized under the EU ETS).

companies.name: Northern Lights JV (Equinor/Shell/TotalEnergies)
companies.what: Runs the world's first full-chain CO2 shipping service: purpose-built 7,500 cbm LCO2 carriers shuttle CO2 from European emitters to its Øygarden receiving terminal in Norway.
companies.signal: First commercial cargo shipped and injected Aug-Sep 2025; fleet of 4 ships (3rd, Northern Phoenix, named Apr 2025 under Bernhard Schulte charter); Phase 2 expansion to >5 Mtpa sanctioned

companies.name: Ecolog
companies.what: Pure-play LCO2 shipping company planning the largest dedicated fleet, using medium-pressure carrier designs to cut transport cost.
companies.signal: Plans 65 vessels on the water by 2035; construction of first ships began Mar 2025 for 2027 delivery

companies.name: Knutsen NYK Carbon Carriers (KNCC)
companies.what: Knutsen-NYK JV commercializing elevated-pressure, ambient-temperature LCO2 tank technology (LCO2-EP) that skips deep refrigeration.
companies.signal: AiPs from ClassNK and ABS for designs up to 40,000 cbm; high-pressure shipping studies with terminal partners

companies.name: Capital Clean Energy Carriers
companies.what: Nasdaq-listed owner that placed the first speculative orders for large ammonia/LCO2-capable low-pressure carriers.
companies.signal: 4x 22,000 cbm LCO2 carriers ordered at HD Hyundai Mipo (2023); first vessel floated out Apr 2025

companies.name: Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL)
companies.what: Operates Japan's demonstration LCO2 carrier for the national CCUS program and invested in Larvik Shipping to build Asia-Pacific CO2 shuttle capability.
companies.signal: Demo LCO2 carrier in service for Japanese CCS trials since 2024; multiple AiPs for larger carriers and floating LCO2 storage

companies.name: Larvik Shipping
companies.what: Norwegian operator that has shipped industrial food-grade CO2 since 1988 — the only company with decades of LCO2 marine operating experience, now applied to CCS.
companies.signal: 35+ years of LCO2 cargo operations; MOL took an ownership stake to access its know-how

companies.name: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE)
companies.what: Dominant shipbuilder for the emerging LCO2 carrier orderbook (HD Hyundai Mipo yard), setting the de facto standard for 22k-40k cbm designs.
companies.signal: Holds the majority of global LCO2 newbuild orders incl. Capital Clean Energy and Greek/Japanese owners

companies.name: CO2next (Gasunie/Vopak/Shell/TotalEnergies)
companies.what: Open-access LCO2 import/buffer terminal at Rotterdam Maasvlakte that will receive ship-borne CO2 and feed it into the Aramis offshore storage trunkline.
companies.signal: Development continuing toward FID alongside Aramis (expected 2026)

companies.name: Dan-Unity CO2
companies.what: Danish JV (Evergas/Ultragas) launched in 2021 as the first dedicated CO2 shipping company, targeting Danish and Icelandic storage trades.
companies.signal: Early MOUs (incl. with Carbfix) but no confirmed newbuild orders or recent activity found in 2024-2026 coverage

variations.name: Rail, barge, and truck CO2 logistics
variations.description: Cryogenic tank trailers, rail tank cars, and inland-waterway barges move liquefied CO2 in small parcels — already routine in the merchant (food-grade) CO2 business and now the bridge for emitters too small or stranded to justify a pipeline, or while pipelines are stuck in permitting.

companies.name: Linde
companies.what: World's largest industrial-gas company; operates the biggest merchant CO2 liquefaction and trucking system, the existing template for small-parcel CO2 logistics.
companies.signal: Decades of merchant CO2 distribution; also a CCS project partner (e.g., contracted storage with ExxonMobil)

companies.name: Air Liquide
companies.what: Runs merchant CO2 liquefaction and truck distribution networks across Europe/US and is building port-side CO2 liquefaction capacity for CCS export chains.
companies.signal: Multiple CO2 liquefaction units tied to North Sea CCS export projects announced 2023-2025

companies.name: Messer
companies.what: Largest privately held industrial gas company; significant merchant CO2 sourcing, liquefaction and trucking in Europe and the Americas.
companies.signal: Long-established CO2 distribution business across 30+ countries

companies.name: Nippon Gases
companies.what: European arm of Nippon Sanso; merchant CO2 logistics operator participating in early ship/rail CO2 supply chains for European CCS clusters.
companies.signal: Operates CO2 liquefaction and distribution across Europe; partner in CCS logistics studies

companies.name: Chart Industries
companies.what: Builds the hardware layer of small-parcel CO2 logistics: cryogenic storage tanks, road trailers, ISO containers and liquefaction skids.
companies.signal: Acquisition by Baker Hughes (~$13.6B, announced Jul 2025) pending/closing 2026, folding CO2 logistics kit into an oilfield major

companies.name: HGK Shipping
companies.what: Europe's largest inland-waterway operator, designing dedicated LCO2 barges to feed Rhine/ARA-region CO2 to Rotterdam/Antwerp export terminals.
companies.signal: Classification-approved inland LCO2 vessel designs unveiled 2023-2024 for German industrial CCS chains

variations.white_space: Few credible CCS-dedicated players because rail/truck costs ~2-4x pipeline at scale, so the mode stays niche (<100 ktpa sources); the opening is standardized LCO2 railcar fleets and transload terminals serving stranded ethanol/biogas plants in the post-Navigator Midwest, and inland-barge feeder systems into Rotterdam/Antwerp hubs — currently served only by food-grade incumbents with no pure-play startup.

variations.name: Onshore saline aquifer storage developers (Class VI projects)
variations.description: Developers characterize sites, obtain Class VI (or state-primacy) injection permits, and drill wells into deep saline formations — the largest and most widely distributed storage resource — selling pore space as a fee-per-tonne disposal service backed by 45Q's $85/t.

companies.name: 1PointFive (Occidental)
companies.what: Building saline sequestration hubs sized for both DAC and industrial CO2, anchored to Oxy's Permian and Gulf Coast land positions.
companies.signal: EPA Class VI permits for Stratos DAC sequestration granted Apr 2025 (first ever for DAC); King Ranch South Texas hub application under review

companies.name: BKV Corporation (dCarbon Ventures)
companies.what: Gas producer running its own CCS business: injects gas-processing CO2 at Barnett Zero and is expanding to additional Texas sites.
companies.signal: Barnett Zero injecting since Nov 2023; second project Cotton Cove (Tarrant Co., TX) with EPA-approved MRV plan Jul 2025

companies.name: ADM
companies.what: Operates the first US commercial-scale saline storage wells (Decatur, Illinois, Mt. Simon sandstone) tied to its corn processing plant.
companies.signal: ~4.5 Mt stored cumulatively; 2024 monitoring-well leak (8,000 t) triggered EPA enforcement; injections resumed Aug 2025 under final EPA order

companies.name: Carbon TerraVault (California Resources)
companies.what: Repurposing California reservoir positions into permitted storage vaults with a Brookfield JV funding development.
companies.signal: Received California's first EPA Class VI permits (CTV I, end-2023); multiple CDMAs signed with emitters

companies.name: Milestone Carbon
companies.what: Sequestration-hub arm of Milestone Environmental Services (largest US energy-waste injection company), developing Permian/Midland Basin saline hubs for gas processors.
companies.signal: Multiple Texas hub sites under development leveraging parent's 40+ injection-well operating record

companies.name: Gulf Coast Sequestration
companies.what: Landowner-led storage hub on the McCall family's SW Louisiana acreage, among the first independent Class VI applicants on the Gulf Coast.
companies.signal: EPA draft Class VI permits issued 2024 for its Calcasieu Parish hub

companies.name: Tenaska
companies.what: Private power developer assembling one of the largest US portfolios of independent CO2 storage hubs (10+ sites across TX, LA, MS, OH and more).
companies.signal: Multiple Class VI applications in EPA/state queues across several states

companies.name: Wabash Carbon Services (Wabash Valley Resources)
companies.what: Holds EPA Class VI permits to store CO2 from its Indiana ammonia/syngas plant in the Mt. Simon formation.
companies.signal: Two Class VI well permits issued 2024; project advancing through financing amid local opposition

companies.name: Vault 44.01
companies.what: Calgary-based end-to-end storage developer holding Alberta carbon sequestration evaluation rights (Rocky Mountain Carbon Vault near Edson; Athabasca Banks hub with Moraine Initiatives).
companies.signal: Awarded Alberta hub evaluation rights; partner on Rocky Mountain Carbon BECCS storage

variations.name: Offshore storage hubs (subsea saline formations and depleted fields)
variations.description: Hub operators combine shared transport (pipelines or ships) with subsea injection wells beneath the seabed, selling open-access storage-as-a-service to industrial clusters — avoiding onshore landowner conflict and serving Europe and Asia where onshore storage is constrained.

companies.name: Northern Lights JV
companies.what: Equinor/Shell/TotalEnergies JV operating the world's first open-access cross-border offshore storage service (Aurora saline formation, 2,600 m under the Norwegian North Sea).
companies.signal: First CO2 injected Aug 2025 (Heidelberg Materials Brevik cement); Phase 2 to >5 Mtpa under EPC with SLB OneSubsea; first storage certificates issued

companies.name: Porthos
companies.what: Port of Rotterdam/Gasunie/EBN JV storing Rotterdam industrial CO2 in the depleted P18 gas field 20 km offshore — the Netherlands' first hub.
companies.signal: ~2.5 Mtpa, fully contracted (Shell, ExxonMobil, Air Liquide, Air Products); operational 2026

companies.name: Aramis (TotalEnergies/Shell/EBN/Gasunie)
companies.what: Next-generation Dutch trunkline hub designed for ~22 Mtpa, taking both piped and shipped CO2 (via CO2next) to offshore storage fields.
companies.signal: Dutch state committed €639M (~$726M); FID expected 2026 with Gasunie/EBN owning the infrastructure

companies.name: Northern Endurance Partnership (bp/Equinor/TotalEnergies)
companies.what: Operates the transport-and-storage backbone for the UK East Coast Cluster, injecting into the Endurance saline aquifer offshore Teesside.
companies.signal: FID Dec 2024 (~£4B with UK government support); ~4 Mtpa initial, operations ~2028

companies.name: Storegga (Acorn)
companies.what: Independent UK developer leading the Acorn hub at St Fergus, Scotland (depleted fields + saline storage) with Shell, Harbour Energy and NSMP.
companies.signal: UK government committed development funding to Acorn in the June 2025 spending review; financial close targeted this Parliament

companies.name: Bayou Bend CCS (Chevron/TotalEnergies/Equinor)
companies.what: One of the largest US offshore/onshore storage positions (~140,000 acres in Texas state waters and Chambers County), Chevron-operated.
companies.signal: Appraisal wells drilled 2023-2024; Equinor bought in via Carbonvert's 25% stake (2024)

companies.name: ExxonMobil
companies.what: Holds the largest US offshore CO2 storage lease (271,000 acres from the Texas General Land Office) complementing its onshore Gulf Coast network.
companies.signal: Record GLO lease executed Oct 2024; >5 Mtpa of emitter contracts feeding its Gulf storage system

companies.name: Petronas
companies.what: Building Kasawari CCS offshore Sarawak — the world's largest dedicated offshore CO2 processing platform (3.3 Mtpa into the M1 depleted field) — and positioning Malaysia as a storage hub for Japanese/Korean CO2 imports.
companies.signal: ~$1B project; platform installed, first injection pulled forward to 2027; Malaysia CCUS Act passed 2025

variations.name: Depleted oil/gas field storage and CO2-EOR transition projects
variations.description: Re-using well-characterized depleted reservoirs (and CO2-EOR fields with existing pipelines and injection kit) cuts appraisal cost and time versus greenfield saline sites, though legacy wellbores add leak-management work; EOR operators are converting infrastructure to pure sequestration as 45Q now pays EOR and storage near-parity.

companies.name: Occidental
companies.what: World's largest CO2-EOR operator (Permian) converting its CO2 pipelines, wells and subsurface expertise into a sequestration and DAC-anchored carbon management business.
companies.signal: Decades injecting ~20+ Mtpa for EOR; Stratos DAC + Class VI sequestration permits Apr 2025

companies.name: Denbury
companies.what: The leading US CO2-EOR specialist and owner of the Gulf Coast 'Green Pipeline'; its network is now the backbone of ExxonMobil's CCS-as-a-service offering.
companies.signal: Acquired by ExxonMobil for $4.9B (Nov 2023) explicitly for its CO2 transport/storage value

companies.name: Santos
companies.what: Operates Moomba CCS, injecting into depleted Cooper Basin gas reservoirs onshore Australia at one of the lowest unit costs of any storage project.
companies.signal: 1.7 Mtpa capacity; injecting since Oct 2024 with high uptime

companies.name: Eni
companies.what: Converting depleted gas fields into storage hubs on two fronts: Ravenna CCS (Adriatic, injecting since Sept 2024) and HyNet/Liverpool Bay in the UK.
companies.signal: HyNet reached financial close Apr 2025 (~£2B UK support; 4.5 Mtpa from ~2028); Ravenna phase 1 operating, targeting 4 Mtpa by 2030

companies.name: INEOS Energy
companies.what: Leads Project Greensand, storing shipped CO2 in the depleted Nini oil field offshore Denmark — the EU's first operational full-scale CO2 storage facility.
companies.signal: World-first cross-border offshore injection pilot Mar 2023; Greensand Future commercial ops from end-2025/early-2026 at 0.4 Mtpa, scaling toward 8 Mtpa by 2030

companies.name: Perenco
companies.what: Developing Project Poseidon in the depleted Leman gas field (UK southern North Sea), re-using its own platforms and wells.
companies.signal: Completed the UK's first offshore CO2 injection test (Leman 27H, 15 cycles) Apr 2025

companies.name: Harbour Energy
companies.what: Developer of Viking CCS, repurposing depleted Rotliegend gas fields off the Humber for up to 15 Mtpa, plus a partner in Acorn.
companies.signal: FEED complete and onshore pipeline DCO granted 2025; awaiting UK Track 2 financial close — timeline risk acknowledged by company

companies.name: CapturePoint
companies.what: Operates CO2-EOR fields in Texas/Louisiana while developing the CENLA dedicated sequestration hub in central Louisiana — a live EOR-to-storage transition play.
companies.signal: CENLA hub Class VI applications advancing under Louisiana primacy; existing EOR injection operations generate cash flow

variations.name: Storage site characterization, modeling, and monitoring tech (seismic, fiber-optic, downhole, satellite)
variations.description: Seismic imaging, distributed fiber-optic sensing, downhole gauges, satellite InSAR and reservoir simulation that prove CO2 stays in the storage complex — mandatory for Class VI/EU permits and 45Q/credit MRV, and the main lever for cutting storage cost and earning public trust (the ADM leak made MMV a board-level issue).

companies.name: SLB
companies.what: End-to-end carbon storage offering from site screening and the Sequestri digital well/reservoir ecosystem to long-term monitoring; deepest CCS subsurface bench in industry.
companies.signal: OneSubsea EPC for Northern Lights Phase 2 (2025); CCS tech deployed on dozens of storage projects

companies.name: Baker Hughes
companies.what: CCUS measurement and digital monitoring (CarbonEdge platform) plus injection wellheads; buying Chart Industries to add CO2 handling hardware.
companies.signal: CarbonEdge launched 2024; strategic CCS partnership with Frontier Infrastructure (2025); Chart acquisition pending

companies.name: Viridien (formerly CGG)
companies.what: Dedicated carbon storage business line: seismic imaging, site screening databases and 4D monitoring design for storage permits.
companies.signal: Storage screening/monitoring contracts across US Gulf Coast, North Sea and Asia-Pacific hubs

companies.name: TGS
companies.what: Multi-client subsurface data giant mapping storage-suitable acreage and selling CO2 storage assessment and OBN-based monitoring packages.
companies.signal: Dedicated CO2 storage mapping/monitoring product line; merged with PGS (2024) adding acquisition fleet

companies.name: MicroSeismic
companies.what: Passive/induced-seismicity specialist whose CO2SeQure service provides real-time plume, fault and seismic-event monitoring for storage sites.
companies.signal: Multiple DOE grants since 2023 to commercialize CO2SeQure; monitoring deployments on US Class VI projects

companies.name: Silixa
companies.what: Distributed acoustic/temperature fiber sensing for CO2 plume tracking and well integrity, proven at CCS field labs (CaMI, Otway) and commercial sites.
companies.signal: Acquired by Luna Innovations (Dec 2023); DAS increasingly specified in Class VI monitoring plans

companies.name: STRYDE
companies.what: bp spinout making the world's smallest/cheapest nodal seismic sensors, enabling dense baseline and repeat 4D surveys over storage sites at a fraction of legacy cost.
companies.signal: Hundreds of thousands of nodes sold globally; used on CCS baseline surveys in Europe, North America and Asia

companies.name: TRE Altamira (CLS Group)
companies.what: Satellite InSAR ground-deformation monitoring — the technique that flagged uplift at In Salah — now sold as low-cost surface MMV for storage sites.
companies.signal: InSAR monitoring used across CCS and injection projects worldwide

companies.name: Battelle
companies.what: Nonprofit R&D house that is the leading US contractor for storage site characterization, Class VI permitting support and DOE CarbonSAFE projects.
companies.signal: Supports dozens of Class VI applications and several CarbonSAFE storage complexes

variations.name: CO2 injection well services and specialty well engineering
variations.description: CO2 wells need corrosion-resistant alloys, CO2-tight cements, dedicated wellheads and subsea injection systems because wet CO2 forms carbonic acid and cold dense-phase injection thermally shocks casing — a specialty niche the oilfield service majors are productizing as Class VI drilling ramps.

companies.name: SLB
companies.what: Sequestri purpose-built CCS well construction portfolio (CO2-rated cements, materials, completions, digital well design) plus OneSubsea subsea CO2 injection systems.
companies.signal: Sequestri launched Nov 2024; Northern Lights Phase 2 subsea injection EPC (2025)

companies.name: Halliburton
companies.what: CO2-resistant cementing systems and CCS well design/integrity services used on Gulf Coast Class VI and EOR-conversion wells.
companies.signal: Active CCS well construction work across US storage projects per 2025 earnings commentary

companies.name: Baker Hughes
companies.what: Carbon capture and injection wellhead systems, CO2 compression trains, and CCS well completions.
companies.signal: Dedicated CCS wellhead product line; Frontier Infrastructure partnership (2025) bundling wells + storage development

companies.name: Expro
companies.what: CCS well testing, CO2 flow metering and well-integrity services adapted from gas well testing — a key niche since CO2 metering underpins 45Q claims.
companies.signal: CCS contracts on UK and US storage projects 2024-2025

companies.name: Vallourec
companies.what: Premium CO2-tight tubulars and casing connections qualified for dense-phase CO2 service, supplied to European CCS wells.
companies.signal: CCS-qualified OCTG product line with deliveries to North Sea storage projects

companies.name: Aker Solutions
companies.what: EPC specialist that delivered the Northern Lights receiving terminal and offshore injection infrastructure — the reference build for CO2 injection facilities.
companies.signal: Northern Lights Phase 1 delivered 2024-2025; follow-on CCS EPC backlog in Norway/UK

companies.name: TechnipFMC
companies.what: Integrated subsea (iEPCI) CO2 injection systems for offshore storage hubs, adapting subsea production hardware to CO2 service.
companies.signal: Subsea CCS awards on UK/North Sea storage developments 2024-2025

variations.white_space: Almost no pure-play startups: oilfield incumbents already own the rigs, cements and metallurgy, and CCS well counts (~10s/year) are too small to support independents yet. Openings exist in Class VI-specialist drilling contractors, CO2-rated P&A/legacy-wellbore remediation around storage complexes (every depleted-field project must fix old wells), and independent CO2 flow metering/verification as 45Q audit scrutiny rises.

variations.name: Novel storage media (in-situ mineralization, CO2 hydrates, enhanced coal-bed storage, engineered caverns)
variations.description: Alternatives to sedimentary pore space: reacting CO2 into solid carbonate in basalt/peridotite (permanent within ~2 years), locking it as solid hydrate under deep-sea pressure/temperature, adsorbing it in coal seams, or engineered caverns — extending storage to geographies without sedimentary basins and offering permanence beyond conventional trapping.

companies.name: Carbfix
companies.what: Icelandic pioneer of dissolved-CO2 injection into basalt, mineralizing >95% of injected CO2 within about two years; stores for Climeworks' Orca/Mammoth DAC plants.
companies.signal: Injecting since 2012; Coda Terminal cross-border shipping + mineral storage hub won a large EU Innovation Fund grant (3 Mtpa design, ~€13/t target storage cost)

companies.what: Omani/UAE startup mineralizing CO2 in peridotite — the most reactive rock on Earth — via water-dissolved injection, targeting low-cost permanent removal.
companies.signal: $37M Series A (Jul 2024, led by Equinor Ventures); ADNOC Fujairah scale-up to 300+ tonnes after a 10-tonne pilot mineralized in under 100 days; Earthshot Prize winner

companies.name: Cella Mineral Storage
companies.what: Developing basalt mineralization storage wells in the Kenyan Rift Valley to pair with East African DAC and geothermal energy.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; partnered with Octavia Carbon on Kenya's first DAC+storage pilot with early Frontier-ecosystem buyer interest

companies.name: CO2 Lock Corp
companies.what: FPX Nickel spinout targeting CO2 mineralization in brucite-rich serpentinite bodies in British Columbia.
companies.signal: Field pilot stage circa 2023-2024; little public progress confirmed since

variations.white_space: Outside mineralization, this is open field: CO2 hydrate storage has zero commercial players (only academic work and PFLOTRAN modeling through 2025) because formation kinetics, monitoring and deep-sea logistics are unsolved; enhanced coal-bed storage died with its 2000s pilots (swelling kills injectivity); salt caverns are unsuitable for permanent CO2 (creep/economics favor storing H2 instead). The realistic opening is geography-driven mineralization — basalt/peridotite provinces in Iceland, Oman/UAE, Kenya, India's Deccan and offshore Cascadia — co-sited with DAC, where conventional saline basins do not exist; a credible hydrate demonstration in Arctic/deepwater sediments would be genuinely novel but needs patient capital.
